title: The genetic code
caption: Sixty-four codons, 61 for amino acids and three stops. The code is degenerate: most amino acids have several codons, often differing only in the third base (all four GGN codons give glycine). Only methionine and tryptophan have one codon each; leucine, serine and arginine have six (shaded).
alt: A table of the 64 mRNA codons arranged by first, second and third base, with the amino acid or stop for each; AUG is marked as the start codon and UAA, UAG and UGA as stops.
description: AUG codes for methionine and is the start codon.
UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.
61 codons code for the 20 amino acids, so most amino acids have more than one.
Methionine and tryptophan have a single codon each; leucine, serine and arginine have six.
The third base often does not matter: GGU, GGC, GGA and GGG all code for glycine.
